# SlopBot skills

SlopBot helps technical newcomers learn SlopArena and take a humanoid fighter from concept or existing assets to a verified persisted package and local play. It is a creator guide, not an asset generator or a general-purpose project coding agent.

## Load the bundle

Use all three skills:

| Skill | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| [slopbot](SKILL.md) | Entry point, project orientation, guided/fast behavior, permissions, handoffs, and progress |
| [slopbot-character](../slopbot-character/SKILL.md) | Approved kit, asset integration, move authoring, iteration, and package/local-play acceptance |
| [slopbot-animation](../slopbot-animation/SKILL.md) | Existing-clip sourcing and bounded corrections with actual-character verification |

Point your assistant's documented skill discovery at this repository's `skills/` directory, or copy these three complete skill directories into its documented skill location, keeping their names and referenced files. Use its documented reload/new-session procedure after changing discovery. SlopBot can load helpers through the skill loader or as sibling files; installing only the entry point leaves a missing-helper blocker.

No installation is needed to try the local files: ask a file-capable assistant to **read `skills/slopbot/SKILL.md` from your clone and follow it**, giving the absolute checkout path. For example:

> Read the SlopBot skill in my SlopArena clone and follow it. Use this clone as the game checkout. Guided mode: I have a rigged humanoid and some attack clips; help me identify the next step.

For concise approved work, request **fast mode**. To continue later, give the project and the relevant `.slopbot/` record or ask to resume that character. Direct helper invocation must still load SlopBot's shared scope, permission and progress rules.

## What you need

- A skill/file-capable assistant for guidance and the selected SlopArena checkout for current documentation and source inspection. The installed skill directory is not the game checkout.
- For character integration and playtesting, the current Unity/.NET prerequisites in [Contributing](../../CONTRIBUTING.md) and actual supported access to the project/editor/runtime. A clean clone does not include all ignored licensed/local art; supply required assets legitimately.
- A usable humanoid model/rig and real clips as you reach those steps. Model generation, rigging and clip sourcing may use external services, but users choose/provide access and confirm licenses. SlopBot does not require a particular asset vendor.
- A supported clip editor or explicit user-operated handoff for bounded animation adaptation. An assistant being able to load skills does not imply Unity/Blender control, paid-service access, or Editor ownership.

Missing tools produce a specific manual handoff or blocker. Required checks are not marked complete until real results can be inspected. Existing project operation/ownership rules apply; tool examples are not permission to bypass them.

## Supported scope

Guided mode explains project concepts as needed; fast mode reduces explanation. Both require bounded approval before mutations and keep the same verification gates. Neither authorizes installation/configuration, spending, unrelated/destructive work, commits/pushes or publication.

The character path includes concept/kit decisions, model/rig/clip handoffs, import/binding, bounded existing-clip adaptation, Slop Editor move work, Training iteration and verified-package/local-play acceptance. Optional supplied/sourced splash art and VFX can be integrated and checked; original art/effect generation is not promised.

The project guide locates current docs and explains the project. Stage/game-mode creation, general repairs/contributions, custom rigs, original motion/full model or rig authoring, engine extensions, online verification, deployment, and publication remain outside this release. Unsupported mechanics pause for a separate task; SlopBot does not silently change the character design.

## Progress and proof

Character progress lives in the selected clone's ignored `.slopbot/<goal-or-package>.md`, not the installed skills or a private BMAD workspace. The [progress contract](references/progress.md) records approved choices, asset references, input-bound observations and the next blocker. Resume reconciles the record against actual changed files; old approval is not a tool lease, and old evidence is not automatically current.

The finish is the complete approved kit with intentionally resolved required slots, valid real bindings, fresh accepted package payloads and exact local roster pins, then local gameplay using that persisted content. A transient editor draft, successful import, compiler result, or old cook alone is not completion.

**Public-release gate:** the [release contract](spec-slopbot-release/spec-slopbot-release.md) requires the next-character run to establish accepted-package/local-play completion. That gate has not been passed by implementing these skill files. The planned fifth-character video is a creation diary, not a tutorial; only the harness/tool path actually exercised may be claimed as verified. There is no independent-newcomer or all-harness execution certification.

Guidance smoke checks exercised a relocated bundle, existing-package orientation, direct animation-helper loading, guided/fast permissions, manual asset/tool handoffs, and resume after a source change. They did not run Unity or complete a fighter.

The [documentation map](../../docs/README.md) remains the entry point for detailed project rules. SlopBot needs no BMAD installation, private skill catalog, private workspace scripts, or author-specific paths.

|---|---|

Stage/mode creation, unrelated repairs/contributions, custom rigs, full model/rig authoring, original-motion/art generation, engine extensions, online verification, deployment, and publishing are outside this release. Do not automate external accounts or asset services merely because the user approved character work. Model generation, rigging, clip sourcing, and optional splash/VFX sources are explicit handoffs with provenance and licensing checks. Use supported available tools for approved integration and bounded clip corrections; no new adapter framework.

# Working with coding assistants

Read root [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) first. Project contracts live in public
`docs/`; maintained workflows live in [skills/](../../skills/README.md).
BMAD, Orca, OMP and T3 Code are optional tools, not contributor prerequisites.

## Discovery

| Setup | Project entry point | Workflow source |
|---|---|---|
| Codex, including Codex in T3 Code | Root `AGENTS.md` | Generated `.agents/skills/` adapters |
| OMP, including OMP in Orca | `.omp/AGENTS.md` → root `AGENTS.md` | Generated `.omp/skills/` adapters |
| Claude Code | Root `CLAUDE.md` → root `AGENTS.md` | Read `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` directly or configure documented skill discovery |
| Other file-capable assistants | Ask it to read root `AGENTS.md` | Read the relevant `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` directly |

Adapters refer back to this checkout; they are not standalone bundles. To install
skills elsewhere, copy complete canonical directories from `skills/`, keeping their
references and `agents/` policy files. Development skills also need this checkout's
docs and source. SlopBot's creator bundle is described in [its guide](../../skills/slopbot/README.md).

Start a fresh session or use the assistant's documented reload after changing
discovery. Confirm the resolved source before relying on a skill. A loader accepting
a skill does not prove that Unity, Blender, a paid service or deployment is available.
Use a concrete manual handoff when a required capability is missing.

OMP started in an enclosing workspace may need `skills.customDirectories` pointed
at this checkout's `.omp/skills`. Keep retired/global alias exclusions in
[.omp/config.yml](../../.omp/config.yml). Avoid rewriting user-level installations
to repair repository routing. Ignored local advisory skills are not dependencies
of the public project workflows.

## Checkout and task scope

Resolve an explicitly supplied checkout first. Validate `src/Shared/SlopArena.Shared.csproj`
and `tests/Shared.Tests/Shared.Tests.csproj` before running game commands. Otherwise
inspect the current Git root; an enclosing workspace is not necessarily the game.
Canonicalize paths with the host's path tools or Python `Path.resolve()`. Set command
`cwd` to the selected game root. An invalid explicit worktree is a blocker, never
permission to substitute another checkout.

Keep optional planning artifacts at their supplied location. Handoffs name the
actual checkout, spec/ticket if any, approved mutations and observable acceptance.
For live Unity work, include the explicit Editor project and coordination protocol.
A worktree or repository symlink does not isolate an Editor or other linked repositories.

Approval covers the agreed task through implementation and verification. A loaded
skill is guidance, not new permission. Preserve unrelated edits; commit, push,
installation and publication keep the boundaries in `AGENTS.md`. Delegate only when
the user or an applicable workflow asks for delegation. Human gamefeel acceptance
remains separate from automated results.

## Unity and offline checks

For Shared/Server checks that do not need a plugin refresh, pass
`-p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true` to `dotnet build`/`dotnet test`. Focused tests do not
need a separate Shared build: their project reference already builds the tested code.

Live Editor automation requires Bun, the installed Unity CLI and the embedded
Pipeline package. Use the shipped `scripts/unity-editor-gateway.ts`, your own caller
identity, and an explicit approved project. The [Unity CLI guide](unity-cli.md) and
[coordination protocol](unity-editor-coordination.md) describe Orca, T3/Codex and
launcher-configured identities. Routine isolated release builds use their release
wrapper instead. Tool installation still requires user approval.

## Maintaining workflows

Edit `skills/` and public docs. Then run:

```bash
python3 tools/sync_agent_skills.py --write
python3 tools/sync_agent_skills.py --check
python3 tools/check_docs.py
```

The generator maintains discovery metadata, explicit invocation policy and the
`.gitignore` allowlist without copying workflow bodies. It refuses to overwrite an
unmanaged adapter. Documentation checks reject stale adapters, broken links,
author-specific paths and known retired workflows in current guidance. Historical
plans and receipts remain records.

# Product

<!-- impeccable:product-schema 1 -->

## Platform

adaptive

## Users

Primary users are friends playing SlopArena online. They need to join a match, understand each fighter quickly, and complete short remote matches without requiring every player to operate hosting or networking infrastructure.

## Product Purpose

SlopArena is an open-source 3D platform fighter built around expressive movement, knockback, compact hero-style kits, and room for unexpected play. The immediate product goal is a playable friends demo that gets real remote feedback on four admitted cooked characters: FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk.

Success means friends can enter a match, understand what happened, and have enough readable, expressive interaction to want another round. Package admission is not treated as proof of kit completeness or player acceptance.

## Positioning

SlopArena's distinctive mechanism is a server-authoritative 60 Hz simulation shared by the Unity client and GameServer. The same deterministic gameplay model supports training, prediction, reconciliation, rollback, and online matches while leaving presentation in the client.

The combat identity combines camera-relative 8-direction movement, jump arcs, double jumps, fast-fall, ledges, Dash, damage percent, Knockback, Hitstun, Hitstop, Combo Influence, Clash, Burst, and compact fighter kits with meaningful recovery, zoning, and finisher choices.

## Operating Context

The primary operating context is Unity 6 on desktop, with a local training flow and online matches through a GameServer. A master server manages browser, lobby, character-select, and results flow; it does not simulate matches.

Players move through the MatchFlow: Server Browser, Lobby Room, Character Select, Countdown, Fight, Results, and Lobby Room. Non-technical players should be able to use an OfficialServer; technical players may use HostAndPlay.

Gameplay runs at 60 Hz. The client renders authoritative state and semantic presentation events; the Shared simulation remains the gameplay authority.

## Capabilities and Constraints

- Each character uses a canonical 16-entry grid: grounded and aerial variants of normals `1`, `2`, `3`, `4` and specials `A`, `E`, `R`, `F`.
- Physical controls are input adapters and are not persisted move identities.
- New characters are package-native. Editable packages live under `client/Unity/Assets/CharacterPackages/<package>/` and cook into immutable runtime artifacts under `content-cooked/<package>/`.
- Match Content Catalogs pin exact package IDs, versions, dependencies, capability versions, and hashes.
- Raw authoring JSON is cook input, not the runtime contract.
- Server-side simulation is authoritative. Unity physics, animation callbacks, VFX, and audio are presentation or authoring aids only.
- Shared simulation code remains free of Unity types and engine physics queries.
- Current admitted demo roster: FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk. Nilus and its legacy character execution path are retired.
- The longer-term Workshop direction permits approved deterministic primitives and package-owned assets, not arbitrary simulation code, native plugins, or direct Unity-path dependencies.
- The current implementation targets Unity 6 desktop. SlopArena also has a separate web presentation surface; the Impeccable platform value `adaptive` records that the product spans these first-party surfaces rather than asserting a mobile-native target.

## Brand Commitments

The shared identity is **low-poly underground toy-fight-club, with DIY internet-game energy**: scavenged construction, chunky silhouettes, curated asset-pack collage, and cool fighting imagery with jokes second. “Toy” is a construction metaphor, not a requirement for literal plastic or cute styling. The website is the strongest existing graphic reference, not a fully approved implementation.

Target graphic primary actions and selection use Action Yellow (`#FFCC22`). Archivo Black is the target shared name-mark and display voice; marketing pairs it with Space Mono. Native short utility labels may use mono where practical, while dense settings and HUD text should remain readable sans. Paper, Ink, and orange values remain local to each surface; existing native orange `#E05C2A` and marketing orange `#F05B35` are retained.

The canonical visual-language guide is `docs/design/visual-language.md`; art conventions remain authoritative for 3D and assets. The sibling repository `../SlopArena-web` is the web graphic reference.

**Status:** SlopArena is unreleased, developed by a solo developer, and is not on Steam. The player-facing identity rollout is implemented. Frontend pages use the user's authored paper background; Home has separate mode/poster/announcement columns. Chat is an absolute user-sized overlay in menus and gameplay and does not influence underlying composition. Settings and match overlays retain readable neutral fields. The separately approved gameplay HUD now has fight-card player panels with clear lives, four paired tickets displaying all eight moves with live ground/air names and effective bindings, shared damage-tier colors, and a persistent target marker with an optional overhead percentage. 3D arenas, existing navigation, gameplay data/authority, and networking are preserved. Connected-room, distributable-player, creator/Ability Lab, website, and release-copy migration are not claimed; the website still has the misleading Steam CTA.

## Evidence on Hand

- `README.md` contains the current product description, four-character demo status, architecture, development setup, and roster summary.
- `CONTEXT.md` defines the canonical domain vocabulary and settled mechanics.
- `docs/plans/2026-09-05-playable-demo-reset.md` defines the current demo priority.
- `docs/design/visual-language.md` defines the shared presentation grammar.
- `content-cooked/` contains cooked runtime artifacts for the admitted packages.
- `client/Unity/Assets/CharacterPackages/` contains package-native authoring sources and asset catalogs.
- The repository has no confirmed testimonials, press claims, benchmark claims, or external player-acceptance evidence. Future surfaces must not fabricate them.

## Product Principles

1. Make the next player action and the last gameplay event immediately understandable.
2. Preserve deterministic, server-authoritative gameplay across local and online paths.
3. Give each fighter a compact, readable identity with meaningful counterplay.
4. Prefer honest prototype energy over generic polish or unsupported claims.
5. Expand creator content through immutable, reviewable, deterministic packages.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

Gameplay and UI must not rely on color alone for status, player identity, or combat information. Preserve readable contrast, stable HUD information, clear focus and confirmation states, and reduced-motion behavior for non-gameplay presentation where the platform supports it.

# Working with coding assistants

Read root [AGENTS.md](../../AGENTS.md) first. Project contracts live in public
`docs/`; maintained workflows live in [skills/](../../skills/README.md).
BMAD, Orca, OMP and T3 Code are optional tools, not contributor prerequisites.

## Discovery

| Setup | Project entry point | Workflow source |
|---|---|---|
| Codex, including Codex in T3 Code | Root `AGENTS.md` | Generated `.agents/skills/` adapters |
| OMP, including OMP in Orca | `.omp/AGENTS.md` → root `AGENTS.md` | Generated `.omp/skills/` adapters |
| Claude Code | Root `CLAUDE.md` → root `AGENTS.md` | Read `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` directly or configure documented skill discovery |
| Other file-capable assistants | Ask it to read root `AGENTS.md` | Read the relevant `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` directly |

Adapters refer back to this checkout; they are not standalone bundles. To install
skills elsewhere, copy complete canonical directories from `skills/`, keeping their
references and `agents/` policy files. Development skills also need this checkout's
docs and source. SlopBot's creator bundle is described in [its guide](../../skills/slopbot/README.md).

Start a fresh session or use the assistant's documented reload after changing
discovery. Confirm the resolved source before relying on a skill. A loader accepting
a skill does not prove that Unity, Blender, a paid service or deployment is available.
Use a concrete manual handoff when a required capability is missing.

OMP started in an enclosing workspace may need `skills.customDirectories` pointed
at this checkout's `.omp/skills`. Keep retired/global alias exclusions in
[.omp/config.yml](../../.omp/config.yml). Avoid rewriting user-level installations
to repair repository routing. Ignored local advisory skills are not dependencies
of the public project workflows.

## Checkout and task scope

Resolve an explicitly supplied checkout first. Validate `src/Shared/SlopArena.Shared.csproj`
and `tests/Shared.Tests/Shared.Tests.csproj` before running game commands. Otherwise
inspect the current Git root; an enclosing workspace is not necessarily the game.
Canonicalize paths with the host's path tools or Python `Path.resolve()`. Set command
`cwd` to the selected game root. An invalid explicit worktree is a blocker, never
permission to substitute another checkout.

Keep optional planning artifacts at their supplied location. Handoffs name the
actual checkout, spec/ticket if any, approved mutations and observable acceptance.
For live Unity work, include the explicit Editor project and coordination protocol.
A worktree or repository symlink does not isolate an Editor or other linked repositories.

Approval covers the agreed task through implementation and verification. A loaded
skill is guidance, not new permission. Preserve unrelated edits; commit, push,
installation and publication keep the boundaries in `AGENTS.md`. Delegate only when
the user or an applicable workflow asks for delegation. Human gamefeel acceptance
remains separate from automated results.

## Unity and offline checks

For Shared/Server checks that do not need a plugin refresh, pass
`-p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true` to `dotnet build`/`dotnet test`. Focused tests do not
need a separate Shared build: their project reference already builds the tested code.

Live Editor automation requires Bun, the installed Unity CLI and the embedded
Pipeline package. Use the shipped `scripts/unity-editor-gateway.ts`, your own caller
identity, and an explicit approved project. The [Unity CLI guide](unity-cli.md) and
[coordination protocol](unity-editor-coordination.md) describe Orca, T3/Codex and
launcher-configured identities. Routine isolated release builds use their release
wrapper instead. Tool installation still requires user approval.

## Maintaining workflows

Edit `skills/` and public docs. Then run:

```bash
python3 tools/sync_agent_skills.py --write
python3 tools/sync_agent_skills.py --check
python3 tools/check_docs.py
```

The generator maintains discovery metadata, explicit invocation policy and the
`.gitignore` allowlist without copying workflow bodies. It refuses to overwrite an
unmanaged adapter. Documentation checks reject stale adapters, broken links,
author-specific paths and known retired workflows in current guidance. Historical
plans and receipts remain records.

- Current admitted demo roster: FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk. Nilus and its legacy character execution path are retired.
- The longer-term Workshop direction permits approved deterministic primitives and package-owned assets, not arbitrary simulation code, native plugins, or direct Unity-path dependencies.
- The current implementation targets Unity 6 desktop. SlopArena also has a separate web presentation surface; the Impeccable platform value `adaptive` records that the product spans these first-party surfaces rather than asserting a mobile-native target.

## Brand Commitments

The shared identity is **low-poly underground toy-fight-club, with DIY internet-game energy**: scavenged construction, chunky silhouettes, curated asset-pack collage, and cool fighting imagery with jokes second. “Toy” is a construction metaphor, not a requirement for literal plastic or cute styling. The website is the strongest existing graphic reference, not a fully approved implementation.

Target graphic primary actions and selection use Action Yellow (`#FFCC22`). Archivo Black is the target shared name-mark and display voice; marketing pairs it with Space Mono. Native short utility labels may use mono where practical, while dense settings and HUD text should remain readable sans. Paper, Ink, and orange values remain local to each surface; existing native orange `#E05C2A` and marketing orange `#F05B35` are retained.

The canonical visual-language guide is `docs/design/visual-language.md`; art conventions remain authoritative for 3D and assets. The sibling repository `../SlopArena-web` is the web graphic reference.

**Status:** SlopArena is unreleased, developed by a solo developer, and is not on Steam. The player-facing identity rollout is implemented. Frontend pages use the user's authored paper background; Home has separate mode/poster/announcement columns. Chat is an absolute user-sized overlay in menus and gameplay and does not influence underlying composition. Settings and match overlays retain readable neutral fields. The separately approved gameplay HUD now has fight-card player panels with clear lives, four paired tickets displaying all eight moves with live ground/air names and effective bindings, shared damage-tier colors, and a persistent target marker with an optional overhead percentage. 3D arenas, existing navigation, gameplay data/authority, and networking are preserved. Connected-room, distributable-player, creator/Ability Lab, website, and release-copy migration are not claimed; the website still has the misleading Steam CTA.

## Evidence on Hand

- `README.md` contains the current product description, four-character demo status, architecture, development setup, and roster summary.
- `CONTEXT.md` defines the canonical domain vocabulary and settled mechanics.
- `docs/plans/2026-09-05-playable-demo-reset.md` defines the current demo priority.
- `docs/design/visual-language.md` defines the shared presentation grammar.
- `content-cooked/` contains cooked runtime artifacts for the admitted packages.
- `client/Unity/Assets/CharacterPackages/` contains package-native authoring sources and asset catalogs.
- The repository has no confirmed testimonials, press claims, benchmark claims, or external player-acceptance evidence. Future surfaces must not fabricate them.

## Product Principles

1. Make the next player action and the last gameplay event immediately understandable.
2. Preserve deterministic, server-authoritative gameplay across local and online paths.
3. Give each fighter a compact, readable identity with meaningful counterplay.
4. Prefer honest prototype energy over generic polish or unsupported claims.
5. Expand creator content through immutable, reviewable, deterministic packages.

## Accessibility & Inclusion

Gameplay and UI must not rely on color alone for status, player identity, or combat information. Preserve readable contrast, stable HUD information, clear focus and confirmation states, and reduced-motion behavior for non-gameplay presentation where the platform supports it.

I'm helping the maintainer of SlopArena (repo at /home/binoui/Projects/SlopArena, a Unity 6 3D platform fighter, public on GitHub) make the repo friendly for onboarding a few friends as contributors/creators. Answer these, citing file paths (and line numbers where useful):

1. **The Unity asset gap.** What exactly is missing from a fresh clone that prevents opening/compiling/playing the Unity client (client/Unity)? Read CONTRIBUTING.md, docs/contributing/unity-setup.md, docs/assets/contributor-inputs.md, docs/assets/credits-and-licenses.md, tools/check_unity_setup.py, and skim .gitignore for excluded asset families. For each missing dependency: is it paid (e.g. Animancer — free vs Pro?), a free-but-non-redistributable pack (Synty, Mixamo, Asset Store, etc.), or the maintainer's own local art? Is there ANY documented path for a contributor to obtain them (shared drive, script, private package, Animancer Lite fallback)? Is there any notion of a "minimal" / "stub" / "placeholder" mode where Unity compiles without the art? Check docs/plans/2026-10-13-contributor-cleanup.md and docs/plans/2026-10-13-unity-dependency-ownership.md and docs/plans/2026-10-13-public-reference-kit.md for planned fixes.

2. **What works with no Unity at all.** List every concrete thing a friend can run with just .NET 8 / Python / Node / a browser: builds/tests, tools in tools/README.md (e.g. KnockbackVisuals, MoveDataReport, self-play, any simulators, generated HTML reports like docs/generated/runtime-architecture.html), scripts/*.sh. For each, give the exact command and whether it's genuinely fun/visual for a newcomer vs. purely maintenance. Note anything that's broken or requires local data not in git.

3. **How does a friend PLAY the game?** Is there a Steam Playtest, a downloadable build, a release page? Check docs/plans/2026-09-25-steam-playtest-integration.md, docs/systems/release-pipeline.md, docs/steam/, branding/discord-sticky.md, and any GitHub release workflow in .github/. Is there a Discord or other community channel documented anywhere? Is there a website (a sibling repo ../SlopArena-web is mentioned in PRODUCT.md — check if it exists at /home/binoui/Projects/SlopArena-web and what URL it deploys to)?

4. Check the `videos/sloparena-explained` directory: what is it (a rendered explainer video? a Remotion project?), is there a rendered file that could be linked/embedded in a README?

Report concisely but completely — I will use this to write a README, so precision matters more than prose. Flag anything where docs contradict each other or look stale.

I'm helping the maintainer of SlopArena (repo at /home/binoui/Projects/SlopArena, a Unity 6 3D platform fighter) write a friendly README for friends who want to contribute/create. I need an honest inventory of each creator-facing workflow and how mature it really is. Read-only; thoroughness: very thorough.

For EACH of the following, report: (a) what it is in one plain-English sentence a non-expert friend would understand, (b) the entry point (skill file, Unity menu item, scene, CLI command, tool), (c) prerequisites (Unity? Blender + Blender MCP? an AI coding assistant? paid services like Meshy/Tripo/Mixamo? local art?), (d) maturity evidence — has it actually been used end-to-end? cite commits (`git log --oneline -- <path> | head`), receipts, evidence files, debriefs, or explicit "not yet verified" statements, (e) whether it's AI-assistant-driven (a skill) or a human-usable tool/UI.

Workflows to cover:

3. **Animation test / animation work** — skills/slopbot-animation, skills/sloparena-animation-authoring, docs/systems/animation-system.md. 7. **Move data / balance tooling** — skills/sloparena-move-data-report, tools/MoveDataReport, scripts/move-data.sh, tools/KnockbackVisuals, any self-play/AI-vs-AI simulation.
8. **Game modes** — docs/design/game-modes.md (recent commit d4fd2032 "record replay contracts and game mode proposals"): proposals only or implemented?
9. **Replays** — docs/plans/2026-10-13-replay-v1-design.md, docs/spec-replay-v1/: implemented or draft?

End with a ranked table: workflow | plain-English pitch | needs Unity? | needs AI assistant? | maturity (proven / used once / spec only) | best entry-point link. Be blunt about maturity; the maintainer wants an honest README, not marketing.

## What is Slop Arena?

A 3D platform fighter (Smash / Rivals of Aether-style) built in Godot 4.6 C#.
Open source, MIT license. No company, no investors, no strings attached.

**Gameplay:**
- Multiple characters with full kits, combos, cooldowns — not just skins
- Game modes: 1v1, 2v2, FFA
- Server-authoritative at 60Hz, tick-based. Netcode-ready from day one

**Project vision:**

Born from seeing too many good PvP games die or get abandoned by their devs.
The goal is simple: a fighting game that's *actually* F2P and *actually* open source.
Built by the community, for the community. Made to last and evolve — no battle pass, no seasonal FOMO, no enshittification.

**Who am I:**

Senior web dev (8+ years), PvP gamer since forever, brand new to game dev.
I vibe-code everything (yes, even the assets). The name "Slop Arena" is ironic — we embrace the chaos.

**Current status:**

Playable sandbox prototype. 1 character (Manki — mad bomber monkey). Combat system, custom FSM, input buffer, aimed charge, HUD/UI — all functional. Network architecture ready. Next up: more characters, matchmaking, real game modes.

GitHub: https://github.com/Binoui/SlopArena

---
name: slopbot-character
description: Plan and complete an approved SlopArena humanoid character package using the project's existing character, Ability Lab, and acceptance workflows.
---

# SlopBot Character

Use this helper for the character work owned by the selected SlopArena checkout. The entry skill `slopbot` owns approvals, interaction mode, selected checkout, and the small `.slopbot/<package-or-goal>.md` progress record. If invoked directly, first load those shared instructions from the harness skill loader or sibling `../slopbot/SKILL.md`; if unavailable, stop rather than bypassing them. Resolve every project document below from the user's selected checkout, never from this installed helper's directory or an author's workspace path. Work only within the approved character scope; a missing tool means an explicit user handoff or blocker, not a claim of action.

## Establish the agreed character and assets

Start with the user's actual goal, existing package/source, approved concept or kit, and progress record. Resume at the unresolved need; do not repeat settled design decisions. If the kit is not approved, use game-root `docs/characters/character-kit-design-principles.md` to agree a humanoid fighter's role, movement/recovery, eight normals, four specials, intended interactions, and desired presentation. Record the decisions and required asset roles before integration. Game-root `docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md` owns implementation and acceptance; `docs/characters/character-import-checklist.md` is a checkpoint, not a substitute.

For every model, rig, animation clip, image, or effect, identify the actual source and exact intended asset; record provenance, creator/source URL or supplier, applicable license, attribution, and whether redistribution into repository/package is permitted. A service/library handoff requires the user to select/provide the assets and licensing evidence. Do not assume a license, generate or fetch assets, author a full model/custom rig/original motion, or silently include non-redistributable content. Preserve source files and Unity `.meta` files. If an ordinary humanoid rig, required clip, license, or supported tool is missing, state the concrete input and expected proof needed from the user; inspect the returned asset before resuming.

Map the concept onto existing gameplay primitives and the current Shared implementation, not an invented mechanic. Confirm a proposed operation/capability is supported by current project documentation/source before relying on it. If an essential interaction is unsupported, name it, pause that branch, and request a separately scoped engine task; present alternatives only as options for approval. Author the agreed package gameplay through existing primitives; do not substitute a different design or extend Shared/server engine code as part of integration.

## Integrate source and author the kit

The project has distinct owners: `package.json` for identity/version/creator/license/attribution/dependencies, `character.json` for gameplay source and presentation IDs, and `CharacterAssetCatalog.asset` for Unity rig and semantic clip bindings. Source package location and the authoring-ready template seam are documented in game-root `docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md` and `docs/systems/ability-lab.md`. Do not invent a package-creation button: current docs identify `AbilityLabPackageWorkspace.NewPackage` as the creation seam but no user-facing creation flow. If no supported tool or authorized operator can invoke that seam, hand off the approved package specification and required result; do not create an ad hoc package or claim creation.

Bind real clips to exact semantic IDs on the actual imported Humanoid rig; preserve unique deterministic pose-track IDs and resolve Avatar/binding diagnostics instead of borrowing another fighter's fallback. If model cleanup or rig repair is needed, name that external/separate scope and route to game-root `docs/characters/character-model-polish.md`. Optional splash art/VFX are supplied/sourced only: verify ownership and the actual consuming surface/binding, and leave them out if not selected. Once selected as required presentation, their integration must be verified rather than silently omitted.

Resolve all sixteen canonical grounded/air slots deliberately from the agreed kit. Approved aliases and move/clip reuse count; a smaller number of independent source entries is not itself an incomplete kit. Use the compiler/inspect resolved projection and approved semantics, not counts or labels alone, to judge coverage. Starter template values are not approved moves. Keep controls/labels distinct from persisted slot identities. Use the existing Slop Editor/Ability Lab Moves workspace for live drafts, timeline, source-stage fields, SceneView overlays, supported operation inspectors, and Undo; do not guess controls or create a second mapping. Through supported Shared/Training paths, observe timing, contact/miss, hitboxes, damage, recovery, movement and selected mechanics; change the relevant draft input and retest. Shared/server owns outcomes; if a mechanic cannot be authored through existing primitives, pause at the engine-task boundary.

## Inspect, cook, admit, and play

Before cooking, resolve supported operations and Editor ownership from game-root `docs/contributing/unity-cli.md`; command examples are not permission to bypass ownership or require an author's private workspace. Discover available supported commands and use `sloparena.character.inspect` read-only on the actual package when authorized. Resolve identity, canonical-slot, source/catalog, rig, dependency, stale-input, and structured diagnostics. If the required tool/owned route is unavailable, hand off the exact package and expected inspect evidence; do not report verification.

Persistence is through the documented Ability Lab **SAVE + COOK** path (or its supported native command flow), not raw edits to generated output. A successful cook must identify the exact current package and its four fresh payloads/hashes; a failed cook is a failure even if it preserves an older valid artifact. Re-inspect after changes and ensure evidence refers to current source, rig, catalog, and dependencies. Do not edit cooked payloads or generated catalog cache as source.

After a successful current cook, complete the applicable focused compiler/catalog/package checks and kit regression evidence specified by game-root `docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md` and `docs/testing.md`. Test, change, and retest behavior that failed or needed tuning; report actual observations and limitations. Add or refresh exact roster admission only through the documented workflow and after required checks/presentation are valid. Verify package identity/version/hashes/dependencies and the exact local roster requirement against fresh content; source-only discovery or a transient draft does not count.

Open the accepted cooked package in Ability Lab to check identity, slot projection, semantic bindings, preview, and diagnostics; exercise Training and applicable local gameplay with that same persisted package. Confirm the roster selects it and the complete agreed kit is actually exercised using admitted content, not an in-memory draft, stale cook, or prior fighter. Record observed checks, input identities/hashes, outcome, and blockers. No online play, publication, or broader release claim follows from local acceptance.

## Resume and handoff

On resume, compare recorded approvals, kit, asset provenance, source/package identity, bindings, cook hashes, roster requirement, and test/play evidence with current files and diagnostics. Invalidate only checks whose inputs changed. Preserve valid prior work. A useful handoff names the exact missing asset/tool/permission, the owner or supported documented route when known, the expected output/evidence, and the next step after it is supplied; never turn instructions into claimed completion.

Lite can be used freely in the Unity Editor, but Pro-only features don't work in runtime builds. The search results mostly describe the v7.4 documentation, plus some v8 alpha-period material, so I couldn't confirm the exact v8 feature list.

entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Check living documentation for broken links and obsolete workflow guidance.

Run from the repository root with ``python3 tools/check_docs.py``. The checker is
intentionally small: it validates paths and a short list of known migration traps,
not generated packet sizes, test totals, or other volatile implementation details.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
from pathlib import Path
from urllib.parse import unquote, urlsplit

import sync_agent_skills

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent

# These are the current instructional surfaces. ADRs, plans, research, generated
# reports, handoffs, and archived tool skills remain records and are not linted for
# present-tense workflow vocabulary.
LIVING_DOCS = {
    Path("README.md"),
    Path("CONTRIBUTING.md"),
    Path("CONTEXT.md"),
    Path("AGENTS.md"),
    Path(".omp/AGENTS.md"),
    Path("docs/README.md"),
    Path("docs/architecture-overview.md"),
    Path("docs/testing.md"),
    Path("docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md"),
    Path("docs/characters/fightguy.md"),
    Path("docs/systems/ability-architecture.md"),
    Path("docs/systems/ability-lab.md"),
    Path("docs/systems/animation-system.md"),
    Path("docs/systems/combat-systems.md"),
    Path("docs/systems/hitstun-di.md"),
    Path("docs/systems/netcode-architecture.md"),
    Path("docs/contributing/conventions.md"),
    Path("docs/contributing/quality.md"),
    Path("docs/contributing/unity-cli.md"),
    Path("docs/contributing/agents.md"),
    Path("docs/contributing/unity-editor-coordination.md"),
    Path("skills/README.md"),
}

CANONICAL_PATHS = {
    "src/Shared",
    "src/Server",
    "tests/Shared.Tests",
    "client/Unity/Assets/CharacterPackages",
    "content-cooked",
    "docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md",
    "docs/characters/fightguy.md",
    "docs/systems/ability-architecture.md",
    "docs/systems/ability-lab.md",
    "docs/systems/animation-system.md",
    "docs/systems/combat-systems.md",
    "docs/systems/netcode-architecture.md",
    "docs/testing.md",
    "docs/contributing/conventions.md",
    "docs/contributing/unity-cli.md",
    "docs/contributing/agents.md",
    "docs/contributing/unity-editor-coordination.md",
    "AGENTS.md",
}

FORBIDDEN_CURRENT_TERMS = (
    (re.compile(r"\bGodot\b|_PhysicsProcess|MoveAndSlide|\bGD\."), "Godot workflow"),
    (re.compile(r"\bBuildFightGuy\b|\bBuild<Name>\b|\bBuildRegistry\b"), "registry factory workflow"),
    (re.compile(r"\bCharacterRegistry\b"), "global character registry workflow"),
    (re.compile(r"\bCharacterDefinition\.cs\b"), "legacy character-definition file workflow"),
    (re.compile(r"\bCharacterAnimationConfig\b"), "universal manual animation-config workflow"),
)

# A forbidden term is acceptable when a living guide explicitly scopes it to the
# legacy path or warns readers not to use it. This keeps migration notices useful.
LEGACY_OR_WARNING = re.compile(
    r"legacy|historical|superseded|deprecated|modification.only|not a template|"
    r"do not|must not|never|avoid|not universal|not a runtime|not current|compatibility|"
    r"\bno\b",
    re.IGNORECASE,
)

AUTHOR_PATH = re.compile(r"file:///|/(?:home|Users)/[^\s/`]+/|[A-Za-z]:[\\/]Users[\\/]")

# Inline Markdown links. Reference-style links are intentionally outside this
# check because their destinations are not recoverable without a full Markdown AST.
MARKDOWN_LINK = re.compile(r"(?<!!)\[[^\]]*\]\(([^)\s]+)(?:\s+[^)]*)?\)")
QUALITY_CODE_BLOCK = re.compile(r"(?m)^```(?:bash|sh)\s*\n(.*?)^```\s*$", re.DOTALL)
QUALITY_COMMAND = re.compile(
    r"(?m)^\s*(?:make\s+(?P<make>[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)|"
    r"dotnet\s+(?:build|test)\s+(?P<dotnet>[^-\s\\][^\s\\]*)|"
    r"python3?\s+-m\s+unittest\s+discover\s+-s\s+(?P<unittest_start>[^\s]+)\s+"
    r"-p\s+['\"]?(?P<unittest_pattern>[^'\"\s]+)|"
    r"python3?\s+(?P<python>[^-\s\\][^\s\\]*)|bun\s+(?P<bun>[^-\s\\][^\s\\]*))"
)
QUALITY_REFERENCED_PATH = re.compile(r"`(?P<path>(?:[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+/)*[A-Za-z0-9_.-]+)`")


def check_quality_commands(errors: list[str], files: list[Path]) -> None:
    source = Path("docs/contributing/quality.md")
    if source not in files:
        return
    text = (ROOT / source).read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
    for match in QUALITY_REFERENCED_PATH.finditer(text):
        target = match.group("path")
        if "/" not in target and not target.endswith((".csproj", ".sln")):
            continue
        if not (ROOT / target).is_file():
            line = text.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1
            errors.append(f"{source}:{line}: missing referenced workflow/script/project {target}")
    for block in QUALITY_CODE_BLOCK.finditer(text):
        for match in QUALITY_COMMAND.finditer(block.group(1)):
            make_target = match.group("make")
            unittest_start = match.group("unittest_start")
            unittest_pattern = match.group("unittest_pattern")
            target = make_target or match.group("dotnet") or match.group("python") or match.group("bun") or unittest_start
            if make_target:
                makefile = ROOT / "Makefile"
                targets: set[str] = set()
                if makefile.is_file():
                    for line in makefile.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines():
                        if line and not line[0].isspace() and ":" in line:
                            targets.update(line.split(":", 1)[0].split())
                exists = make_target in targets
            elif unittest_start:
                test_dir = ROOT / unittest_start
                exists = test_dir.is_dir() and any(path.is_file() for path in test_dir.glob(unittest_pattern))
            elif match.group("python") or match.group("bun") or target.endswith((".csproj", ".sln")):
                exists = (ROOT / target).is_file()
            else:
                exists = (ROOT / target).is_dir()
            if not exists:
                line = text.count("\n", 0, block.start(1) + match.start()) + 1
                errors.append(f"{source}:{line}: missing executable target/path {target}")

# SLOPArena

**An open-source 3D platform fighter built around expressive movement, knockback, and compact hero-style kits.**

SLOPArena takes the platform-fighter fundamentals of movement, damage percent, recovery, edge pressure, and launching opponents off the stage, then gives each fighter a small set of distinctive specials and tools to play around.

The goal is a game that is readable and competitive without taking itself too seriously: strong character identities, generous 3D hitboxes, expressive movement, and plenty of room for stupid things to happen.

SLOPArena takes the platform-fighter fundamentals of movement, damage percent, recovery, edge pressure, and launching opponents off the stage, then gives each fighter a small set of distinctive specials and tools to play around.

The goal is a game that is readable and competitive without taking itself too seriously: strong character identities, generous 3D hitboxes, expressive movement, and plenty of room for stupid things to happen.

> **Current state:** SLOPArena is working toward a playable friends demo with four fighters: FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk. Their kits are still being tuned and playtested. See the [playable friends demo plan](docs/plans/2026-09-05-playable-demo-reset.md) for current product work.

## docs/friends-onboarding
--- tools/README (origin) ---
# Project tools

The root [SlopArena.sln](../SlopArena.sln) is the maintained .NET build set:
Shared, Server, their tests, and the C# tools below. CI builds all of them. Tools
reuse Shared and the admitted cooked packages; editing raw package source alone
does not change a report's runtime input.

```bash
dotnet build SlopArena.sln --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
dotnet test SlopArena.sln --no-build --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
```

To run one tool without copying the Shared plugin into Unity:

```bash
dotnet run --project tools/BonkInvestigation -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true -- <output-directory>
```

Use each tool's argument parser or documented usage before running it. Supply an
ignored output directory for reports. Baking tools write content and need a
deliberately selected destination; build success does not authorize overwriting
current arena data. A tool's successful run is diagnostic evidence, not acceptance
of a fighter or a networked match.

| Project | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `BakeArenas.csproj` | Offline arena generation; select the output directory explicitly |
| `AssetCatalog/` | Query the offline environment catalog and prepare asset worksets |
| `MoveDataReport/` | Authored timings, simulated trajectories and contact coverage |
| `MovementReport/` | Ground/air movement measurements |
| `AerialProfileReport/` | Fighter aerial movement and attack profiles |
| `AerialApproachReport/` | Aerial approach, landing and slide-flow diagnostics |
| `AbDiffReport/` | Compare baseline and counterfactual simulation/tuning outcomes |
| `SelfPlayReport/` | Deterministic bot-match diagnostics |
| `BonkInvestigation/` | Sword contact, pose-phase and grounded move/jump recovery diagnostics |
| `SpectateView/` | Record and inspect deterministic matches |

[KnockbackVisuals](KnockbackVisuals/README.md) supplies a browser viewer for saved
trajectory comparisons. `skill-evals/` is separate TypeScript session-analysis
tooling; see its [README](skill-evals/README.md). Python documentation and adapter
checks are documented in [quality checks](../docs/contributing/quality.md).

[`check_unity_setup.py`](check_unity_setup.py) inspects installed embedded
packages, pinned managed DLLs and folder ownership, the Shared plugin, and four character catalogs'
GUID inputs without operating Unity. Run `python3 tools/check_unity_setup.py`,
optionally with `--root /path/to/checkout --json`. See
[Unity setup](../docs/contributing/unity-setup.md) for scope and provisioning.

[`unity_asset_bundle.py`](unity_asset_bundle.py) exports ignored Unity inputs and
their metadata to a private ZIP for another development machine. Its importer
verifies checksums and tracked metadata, and preserves conflicting laptop files.
See the [private installation transfer](../docs/contributing/unity-setup.md#copying-an-existing-private-asset-installation)
for commands; Git and Python 3.9 or newer are sufficient.

The historical `research/flight-sweep/` experiment has been removed; restore it
with `git checkout d98c6c26 -- research/flight-sweep` if that research becomes
relevant. Generated visual reports and archived investigations remain evidence
for their source snapshot.

Add a new maintained C# tool to `SlopArena.sln` and this inventory so CI compiles
it. Document its inputs and output directory. Keep exploratory projects outside
that build set until they have a maintained purpose.

Unity editor tools live under `client/Unity/Assets/Scripts/Editor/` and
`client/Unity/Assets/AbilityLab/Editor/`. Their supported authoring and verification
paths are described in [Unity CLI](../docs/contributing/unity-cli.md),
[Ability Lab](../docs/systems/ability-lab.md), and
[character authoring](../docs/characters/adding-a-new-character.md).
See [Unity tools](../docs/contributing/unity-tools.md) for menu groups and package
test input/output preservation.

Original procedural environment art lives under [blender/](blender/README.md).
The retained FightGuy Sanctuary generator includes reusable mesh construction,
rock/scenery generation, ambient-occlusion baking, Unity FBX export and camera
preview techniques. Its reuse guide identifies stage-specific assumptions; these
Python art tools are separate from the .NET solution above.

# SLOPArena — how to play

1. Download `SLOPArena-<version>.zip` from the release page.
2. Right-click the zip → Extract All. Keep the extracted folder together.
3. Open the folder and double-click `SLOPArena.exe`.
   - Windows shows "Windows protected your PC" → click "More info" → "Run anyway".
     (The game isn't code-signed yet; this is normal.)
4. Main menu:
   - **Training** — play solo against bots, try every character.
   - **Join** — pick a server (e.g. "SLOPArena EU #1"), enter the lobby, ready up.
     Your friend does the same; the host starts when everyone is ready.
5. Controls:
   - Mouse — aim camera
   - WASD — move
   - Space — jump (double-tap for double jump)
   - Shift — dash
   - Left click — attack
   - Right click — ability 1
   - Q / E / R / F — abilities 2-5
   - Esc — pause / back
6. Problems?
   - Game won't start → your PC must be 64-bit Windows 10/11.
   - Firewall prompt → allow SLOPArena on private networks.
   - Can't see any servers → the online part is a friends demo; ask the host
     if the servers are up.

content.content:
# Knockback visual comparison

Watch before/after knockback paths from the real Shared simulation, with synchronized playback, a time scrubber, and selectors for all four characters, individual normal hits, and damage percents. Orange is before; teal is after. Ordinary views use equal horizontal and vertical distance scale. The weak-pop close-up magnifies height five times and labels that magnification.

## Open the saved viewer

From the repository root:

```bash
python3 tools/KnockbackVisuals/serve.py
```

Open **http://localhost:8765/**. It opens the latest saved comparison; page links switch between the original flight update and the outlier/special tuning. Use `--view original` or `--view outliers` to choose explicitly. Stop the server with Ctrl+C; use `--port 8766` if the default port is busy. The launcher resolves the viewer location from its own file, so it also works from another working directory.

You can also open [the standalone HTML](../../docs/generated/knockback-visuals/index.html) directly in a browser. It embeds every trajectory and requires no server, internet, Unity, or JavaScript packages. The [overview](../../docs/generated/knockback-visuals/overview.png), [animation](../../docs/generated/knockback-visuals/before-after.mp4), and [measurement report](../../docs/generated/knockback-flight-comparison.md) accompany the interactive viewer.

## Saved comparison

`comparison.json` preserves both sides of the **2026-10-11 flight-physics comparison**, including the baseline simulation hash, recording conditions, and trajectory point columns. It is a historical snapshot; editing the simulation does not silently change either side. It contains all four characters at 0%, 60%, 120%, and 200% damage before the hit, including isolated entries for multihit normals. Positions are rounded to five decimal places for visualization.

Both datasets use the same cooked move definitions. Victims are passive, with no DI, SDI, player movement, or follow-up hits; hitstop is excluded. Downward sends start above the floor. Ground contact can occur while hitstun continues, and positions stop at the end of the original report rather than extrapolating later ground carry. See the measurement report for the full method and verification.

The viewer, snapshot, template, generator, PNG, and MP4 live in normal repository paths, outside ignored artifact directories.

`outliers-comparison.json` preserves the subsequent authoring pass under the new flight model. Its [viewer](../../docs/generated/knockback-outlier-visuals/index.html) includes all normal and special hit components, projectile/explosion sends, fixed hitstun, and Dash Slash charge tiers. Components are isolated; they are not a complete special sequence. Its [report](../../docs/generated/knockback-outlier-tuning.md) records the changes and actual-contact verification.

## Regenerate

Rebuild the standalone HTML from the saved snapshot using Python's standard library:

```bash
python3 tools/KnockbackVisuals/generate.py
python3 tools/KnockbackVisuals/generate.py \
  --comparison tools/KnockbackVisuals/outliers-comparison.json \
  --output docs/generated/knockback-outlier-visuals
```

To regenerate the PNG and MP4 too, install Matplotlib in a local virtual environment and have `ffmpeg` on your PATH:

```bash

overview.png
hud-preview.css

- camera-relative 8-direction movement, jump arcs, double jumps, fast-fall, ledges, and Dash;
- Smash-style damage percent, Knockback, Hitstun, Hitstop, Combo Influence, Clash, and Burst;
- readable hero kits with generous 3D hitboxes and meaningful recovery, zoning, and finisher choices;
- a server-authoritative GameServer for online matches and a local Shared simulation for prediction and training.

Each kit has a canonical **16-entry grid**: grounded and aerial variants for normals `1`, `2`, `3`, `4` and specials `A`, `E`, `R`, `F`. `LMB` and `RMB` are not persisted move identities; physical controls map to the canonical slots through the client input layer.

Solo uses an attacking CPU at the selected difficulty. Training starts with one idle CPU and keeps its controls visible on the HUD. Press Escape or controller Start to adjust Idle, Attack, Shield, or Avoid behavior, difficulty, and damage, or reset damage and positions. Turn off “Show during play” to hide the panel during gameplay; it always appears while paused.

### Gamepad controls

Left Stick moves; Right Stick controls the camera and ability aim. Face buttons South/East/West/North use normals 1/2/3/4; hold LB with those buttons for specials A/E/R/F. The selected move stays fixed until its face button is released. RB jumps, LT crouches/slides/fast-falls, RT dashes, D-pad Left bursts, L3 faces the camera, R3 toggles target lock, and Start pauses. Remap buttons and the special modifier under Settings → Controls → Controller.

content.content:
## Development

The game is built in **Unity 6** with a pure C# simulation shared by the client and GameServer. The simulation advances at **60 Hz**, keeps gameplay deterministic, and supports client prediction with server reconciliation and rollback.

### Quick start

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Binoui/SlopArena.git
cd SlopArena
```

Install .NET SDK 8 to work on the simulation, server, or C# tools. A clean clone
supports these checks without Unity or the local art installation:

```bash
dotnet build SlopArena.sln --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
dotnet test SlopArena.sln --no-build --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true
```

The root solution also supports ordinary C# IDE navigation. See the
[tool inventory](tools/README.md) for the maintained command-line tools.

The Unity client requires Unity `6000.0.78f1`, the separately installed
Animancer package, and exact local rig/animation/presentation assets. A stock
clone cannot compile and play the complete client. Follow the
[Unity setup instructions](CONTRIBUTING.md#unity-client-and-authoring) before
opening the project; Shared must be built for Unity after those prerequisites
are available.

Run the development GameServer from the repository root:

```bash
dotnet run --project src/Server/ -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true -- src/Server/server.json
```

Its development configuration expects a local Master server for registration.
See the [local stack](deploy/local/README.md) for the separate Master checkout
and integration setup.

Explore the [knockback visual comparison](tools/KnockbackVisuals/README.md) to watch saved before/after trajectories for all four fighters. Run `python3 tools/KnockbackVisuals/serve.py` and open http://localhost:8765/, or open the standalone HTML directly in a browser.

## Architecture in one view

```text
Unity client ── input ──► Shared ServerSimulation ◄── input/state ── GameServer
     │                            │
     └── render authoritative state/events

Editable Character Package
  package.json + character.json + CharacterAssetCatalog.asset
                    │
                    ▼
       Shared compiler + Unity asset cook
                    │
                    ▼
Immutable content-cooked package
  manifest + runtime definition + poses + client bindings
```

# SlopBot skills

SlopBot helps technical newcomers learn SLOPArena and take a humanoid fighter from concept or existing assets to a verified persisted package and local play. It is a creator guide, not an asset generator or a general-purpose project coding agent.

## Load the bundle

Use all three skills:

| Skill | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| [slopbot](SKILL.md) | Entry point, project orientation, guided/fast behavior, permissions, handoffs, and progress |
| [slopbot-character](../slopbot-character/SKILL.md) | Approved kit, asset integration, move authoring, iteration, and package/local-play acceptance |
| [slopbot-animation](../slopbot-animation/SKILL.md) | Existing-clip sourcing and bounded corrections with actual-character verification |

Point your assistant's documented skill discovery at this repository's `skills/` directory, or copy these three complete skill directories into its documented skill location, keeping their names and referenced files. Use its documented reload/new-session procedure after changing discovery. SlopBot can load helpers through the skill loader or as sibling files; installing only the entry point leaves a missing-helper blocker.

No installation is needed to try the local files: ask a file-capable assistant to **read `skills/slopbot/SKILL.md` from your clone and follow it**, giving the absolute checkout path. For example:

> Read the SlopBot skill in my SLOPArena clone and follow it. Use this clone as the game checkout. Guided mode: I have a rigged humanoid and some attack clips; help me identify the next step.

For concise approved work, request **fast mode**. To continue later, give the project and the relevant `.slopbot/` record or ask to resume that character. Direct helper invocation must still load SlopBot's shared scope, permission and progress rules.

## What you need

- A skill/file-capable assistant for guidance and the selected SLOPArena checkout for current documentation and source inspection. The installed skill directory is not the game checkout.

## Overview

SLOPArena characters use two complementary layers of attacks:

* **8 normals** on `1 / 2 / 3 / 4`, with grounded and aerial variants.
* **4 specials** on `A / E / R / F`.

Normals provide the character's fundamental fighting-game moveset.

Specials provide character identity, unusual movement, utility, setup, and larger gameplay moments.

Training and Arcade modes work offline, but online matches depend on the server being up, which is worth flagging via Discord. Designing a stage is another option: pitch an idea, block it out with an AI helper, bake collision, add art, and test it in Training. Every existing stage went through this exact workflow, and stage art can even be generated procedurally in Blender.

# SLOPArena **A free, open-source 3D platform fighter: rack up damage, then launch your friends off the stage.** ## Hi! > **TODO (Binoui):** your intro goes here, in your own words. ## What is SLOPArena? It's a platform fighter in the Smash family, in full 3D. Every hit adds damage, and the more damage you carry, the farther you fly, until somebody goes off the stage. Each fighter has a compact kit: eight normal attacks (four on the ground, four in the air) and four specials.

- **Four fighters:** FightGuy, Manki, Wibou, and Bonk. - **Six stages** to pick from, including the three above. - **Training** against a CPU you can tune, and offline **Arcade** challenges. - **Online matches** on a dedicated server, with rollback netcode. - Built in **Unity 6**. The gameplay itself is a deterministic C# simulation that the game and the server share. - **MIT licensed.** Made by one developer and a lot of AI help ([how AI is used](#ai-usage)). > **Where it's at (October 2026):** early. We're building toward a playable demo for friends. The fighters are still being tuned, no stage has had a proper group playtest yet, and making online matches reliable is the current focus. Expect rough edges, and please tell us about them. ### The fighters | Fighter | Style | | --- | --- | | [**FightGuy**](docs/characters/fightguy.md) | Close-range martial artist: Ki Shot, Rising Dragon, Cyclone Kick, and Fist of Fury | | [**Manki**](docs/characters/manki.md) | Pyromaniac inventor monkey with a jetpack, a bazooka, bombs, and aerosol traps | | [**Wibou**](docs/characters/wibou.md) | Kitsune swordswoman who controls space with her blade, then juggles you in the air | | [**Bonk**](docs/characters/bonk.md) | Greatsword bruiser with long reach, a jump-slam recovery, and Blade Storm | ## Things you can do here ### Play it SLOPArena runs on Windows 10 and 11. The easiest way in is the Steam Playtest: ask Binoui for access. Test builds are also attached to the [Releases page](https://github.com/Binoui/SLOPArena/releases). Training and Arcade work offline. Online matches need our server to be up, and they're what we're fixing right now, so they may not connect yet. The controls are [below](#controls). ### Try it in five minutes, no Unity needed Install Git and the [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0), then: ```bash git clone https://github.com/Binoui/SLOPArena.git cd SLOPArena # Watch two CPU fighters brawl in your terminal (Ctrl+C to quit) dotnet run --project tools/SpectateView -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true -- --char manki # Build everything and run the test suite dotnet build SlopArena.sln --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true dotnet test SlopArena.sln --no-build --nologo -p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true ``` That's the real game simulation running with no graphics attached. `-p:SkipUnityPluginCopy=true` keeps these commands from touching the Unity project. More things that work straight from a clone: - **Knockback viewer:** run `python3 tools/KnockbackVisuals/serve.py` and open http://localhost:8765/ to scrub through real launch trajectories for every fighter ([details](tools/KnockbackVisuals/README.md)). - **HUD preview:** run `python3 -m http.server 8000` from the repository root and open http://localhost:8000/tools/hud-preview/ to edit the in-game HUD stylesheet and see the result live. A few icons are missing from a clean clone. - **Reports:** frame data, movement stats, and bot-vs-bot match stats from the command line. See the [tool inventory](tools/README.md). ### Make stuff These need the full Unity project, which isn't self-serve yet (see [Getting set up](#getting-set-up)). They're where most of the fun is, and some of them start with no setup at all. **Make your own fighter.** SlopBot is an AI guide that takes you from an idea to a playable fighter: kit design, model and animation handoffs, wiring up the moves, and testing them in Training. The design part needs no Unity, so you can start today. SlopBot is brand new and nobody has finished a fighter with it yet, so you'd be the first. See [Working with an AI assistant](#working-with-an-ai-assistant) to start it, and the [kit design principles](docs/characters/character-kit-design-principles.md) for what makes a good fighter. **Design a stage.** Pitch an idea, block it out in grey boxes with an AI helper, then bake the collision, dress it with art, and test it in Training. Every current stage was made this way, and stage art can also be generated in Blender with scripts. Start with the [stage concepts](docs/design/stage-concepts.md) and the [stage design workflow](skills/sloparena-stage-design/SKILL.md). **Test and tune moves and animations.** Ability Lab is the in-Unity editor for fighters: scrub any attack frame by frame, see and drag hitboxes, change timings, and try hits against an idle or shielding dummy. It's also where new animations get checked on the real character. See the [Ability Lab guide](docs/systems/ability-lab.md) and the [animation workflow](skills/sloparena-animation-authoring/SKILL.md). **Fix up a 3D model.** An AI assistant connected to Blender can clean up shading, holes, and skin weights on a rigged character, with before-and-after comparisons. See the [model polish guide](docs/characters/character-model-polish.md). ### Everything else Ideas, fighter designs on paper, art, VFX, sound, UI, docs, and "this felt bad when I played it" are all welcome. Open an issue ([bug report](https://github.com/Binoui/SLOPArena/issues/new?template=bug_report.yml) or [idea](https://github.com/Binoui/SLOPArena/issues/new?template=feature_request.yml)) or come say hi. New multiplayer modes such as capture zones, volleyball, and crown are [still just ideas](docs/design/game-modes.md), so come argue about them. ## Getting set up | Setup | What you get | What you need | | --- | --- | --- | | **Code only** | Build, tests, simulation tools, engine and server work | Git and the [.NET 8 SDK](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet/8.0); Python 3 for the viewers | | **Full Unity project** | The game in the Unity Editor, Ability Lab, fighters, stages | Unity `6000.0.78f1`, the Animancer package, and art that isn't in Git | **About the Unity project:** some of the art comes from paid asset packs that can't go on GitHub, and the animation library (Animancer) is installed separately, so a fresh clone can't open the full game yet. Talk to Binoui before you spend an evening on it. The [Unity setup guide](docs/contributing/unity-setup.md) has the details, and `python3 tools/check_unity_setup.py` lists what's missing. Open your assistant in the cloned folder and paste one of these: - **Get oriented:** "Read README.md, AGENTS.md, and docs/README.md, then give me a short tour of SLOPArena and suggest a first thing to try. Write one self-contained document with inline <style> and <script>. Local images written as absolute file paths (src="/abs/shot.png", CSS url(/abs/bg.webp), or a JS string) are inlined automatically; remote http(s) URLs, such as a CDN chart library, load as-is. entries.name: mcp__t3-code__html_render
entries.description: Show a finished HTML page (chart, table, diagram, collage, mockup) inline in this thread, above your final text reply; call it before writing that reply. The reader already sees the page, so the reply should not announce it, say where it is, or restate it: add only what the page doesn't say. Preview with html_preview first. T3 fits the frame to the page's height at each reader's width. A height below the page's contentHeight caps the frame there, and the rest scrolls inside it. Write one self-contained document with inline <style> and <script>. Local images written as absolute file paths (src="/abs/shot.png", CSS url(/abs/bg.webp), or a JS string) are inlined automatically; remote http(s) URLs, such as a CDN chart library, load as-is. The frame is borderless on the thread's background, as wide as the reply column (728px on desktop by default, wider if the reader widens chat, about 360px on phones), and its left edge lines up with your reply text. The page sits on the thread's own background, so by default leave html, body, and the outermost element with no background color. This overrides general style preferences such as a fixed black page background. Use a fluid width with no horizontal padding on the outermost element, and no outer card, border, or banner title: the page is part of your reply. If a box needs its own background (a mock of a specific screen, a panel that must stand apart), give it at least 16px of padding on every side and var(--radius) corners, so content never touches its edge. Give charts fixed pixel heights rather than heights that scale with width. Let content set the page's height. Avoid viewport-based heights such as 100vh or height:100% on html or body; the frame grows to fit the page, so they can make it grow again and again. T3 injects its active theme as CSS custom properties on :root, and they follow the user's theme and light/dark mode live: --background (page background, identical to the thread around the frame), --foreground, --muted, --muted-foreground, --card, --card-foreground, --popover, --popover-foreground, --secondary, --secondary-foreground, --border, --input, --ring, --primary, --primary-foreground (solid buttons), --accent, --accent-foreground (brand accent), --accent-surface, --accent-surface-foreground, --destructive, --destructive-foreground, --destructive-surface, --warning, --warning-foreground, --warning-surface, --success, --success-foreground, --info, --info-foreground, --code-background, --code-foreground, --chart-1 ... --chart-6 (categorical series for charts), --radius, --font-sans, --font-mono. The base stylesheet sets html background/color/font from these, body margin to 0, and hides the page's scrollbar; your own CSS overrides it.

height.description: The frame height in CSS pixels, 80-2000. Use html_preview's contentHeight, or less to make long content scroll inside the frame.
